title: `floor` and `ceil` of a double return a `BIGINT`
verdict: a `BIGINT`, not a double: no `-0.0`, no NaN or ±inf; the writer casts back to a double
description: `floor(x)` and `ceil(x)` of a `DOUBLE` return a `BIGINT` (`typeof(ceil(CAST(-0.4 AS DOUBLE)))` is `bigint`), so a negative value above `-1` has a `ceil` of `0` without a sign, and `CAST(ceil(-0.4) AS DOUBLE)` is `+0.0`. The other engines return a double: DuckDB and Polars give IEEE's `-0.0` there (duckdb-R15-round, polars-round). NaN, ±inf and values past 64 bits are spark-round's (SP-5).
reference: `floor` and `ceil` are doubles to doubles (`UnFn.ffloor`, `UnFn.fceil`); the sign of a zero result is `round_zero_sign`, which the reference leaves open (`eval` gives `+0.0`). Spark's writer casts the `BIGINT` back to a double for doubles below `2⁵²` and keeps the others (`sverify.sql.spark`, `whole`), which gives the reference's `+0.0`.

provenance.checked_by: canon PR session (claude/canon-congruence), Spark 4.3.0 local session (sverify.spark_engine.session), Python 3.12 in python/.venv

evidence.sql: SELECT typeof(round(CAST(-0.4 AS DOUBLE))), typeof(ceil(CAST(-0.4 AS DOUBLE)))
SELECT ceil(x), CAST(ceil(x) AS DOUBLE) FROM VALUES (CAST(-0.4 AS DOUBLE)), (CAST(-0.04 AS DOUBLE)), (CAST(-0.6 AS DOUBLE)) AS t(x)
evidence.observed: (0, 0.0), (0, 0.0), (0, 0.0); every 0.0 has a positive sign bit

notes: spark.sql.ansi.enabled true. Recorded apart from spark-round, which also says that `floor` and `ceil` return `BIGINT`, so that the type and the zero's sign stay two findings (theory advisor, 2026-11-09).
